Launch HN: Discovered Materials (YC P26) – AI agents to discover new materials (discoveredmaterials.com)
132 points by advaith08 22 hours ago | hide | past | favorite | 28 comments

Hey HN, we're Advaith and Akash from Discovered Materials ( https://discoveredmaterials.com/ ). We build AI agents that discover new materials for the semiconductor industry.

GPUs today have a heat problem. Nvidia & AMD are almost doubling the TDP (Thermal Design Power) in every chip they release - the H100 (released 2022) has a TDP of 700W, Blackwell (2024) gives out 1.2 kW and Rubin (2026) gives out at 2.3 kW of heat. This trend is expected to continue, and getting rid of this heat is one of the major reasons datacenters consume so much power and water today - they need it to keep chips cool during operation.

The amount of heat produced by a chip and its ability to dissipate it are both influenced by the materials used to make it. For example, we could reduce the energy per bit required to move data between logic and memory by 10-50x by 3D packaging chips (placing HBM memory stacks directly on top of logic chips, instead of placing them beside logic on a 2D circuit board). However, we're unable to do this today because the dielectric material used in HBM (such as SiO2) is a very poor thermal conductor, trapping heat between logic and memory and causing drastic temperature rise during operation. Similarly, there's many other materials in the GPU that are being re-evaluated today - 2 more examples are thermal interface materials and substrates. However, getting a new material into a fab takes years and hundreds of millions of dollars of research - the infamous "lab-to-fab valley of death".

At Discovered Materials, we're optimistic that AI agents can reduce the timeline and cost required to introduce new materials into semiconductor chips. We're seeing glimpses of this already - we tested 7 models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Kimi, and found that they're all able to computationally discover new materials that are dynamically stable and possess promising properties. This was surprising to us - it would generally take a PhD student a couple of weeks of work to discover the kind of materials that these models find over an 8 hour run!

However, computational discovery is the easy part. A material discovery is only valid if the material can be made and tested in a lab (As an example, graphene’s properties were predicted in 1947 but it was made for the first time in 2004). Today’s models are not good at coming up with synthesis recipes to make materials in a lab. Even if they do get better at it, we're uncertain about how much that will help - making a new material is a highly empirical process involving trial and error over many experiments. Human experts themselves cannot "one-shot" the task, but we expect that a highly capable model will reduce the number of experimental iterations required to make a new material. We’ve seen some evidence of this over the 3 months of our Y Combinator batch - we simulated, synthesized and tested thermal interface materials (TIMs) that match the performance of TIMs the world's largest chemical companies have guarded as trade secrets for over 20 years.

We’re releasing hundreds of hundreds of new materials discovered by frontier AI models, as well as our benchmark which measures model ability on material discovery here (also linked in the thread url): https://discoveredmaterials.com/research. It covers what we discuss above, as well as a variety of strange behavior that we observe from the models, such as Claude's propensity to reward hack or GPT-5.6 occasionally losing its mind after ~50M tokens.

Our business model: We aim to license and sell IP on the materials we discover, as well as the IP on how to make these materials. We're also exploring an alternate business model where we sell the harness+tools we use to discover materials to semiconductor and chemical companies, allowing them to discover materials on their own. We're leaning towards the latter to start, but we expect that we'll do both in the long run.

Our backstory: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford University, and has spent the last 11 years studying new materials for semiconductor chips. His work on new nanoscale interconnects was Stanford Engineering’s most popular story of 2025. Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and was a research engineer building video models and agents at Persona AI (acquired) and Luma Labs.

We are very interested in your opinion! The semiconductor industry is quite secretive, and your thoughts on the roadmap of the industry or the materials we should go after would be very helpful. We would also love to hear from people who have run experiments in labs - what can we learn from your experience doing empirical science?

sentences.zh: 这种趋势预计将持续下去，而消除这种热量是当今数据中心消耗大量电力和水的主要原因之一——他们需要它来保持芯片在运行过程中冷却。芯片产生的热量及其散发热量的能力都受到制造它的材料的影响。

sentences.en: For example, we could reduce the energy per bit required to move data between logic and memory by 10-50x by 3D packaging chips (placing HBM memory stacks directly on top of logic chips, instead of placing them beside logic on a 2D circuit board).
sentences.zh: 例如，我们可以通过 3D 封装芯片（将 HBM​​ 内存堆栈直接放置在逻辑芯片顶部，而不是将它们放置在 2D 电路板上的逻辑旁边）将逻辑和内存之间移动数据所需的每比特能量减少 10-50 倍。

sentences.en: However, we're unable to do this today because the dielectric material used in HBM (such as SiO2) is a very poor thermal conductor, trapping heat between logic and memory and causing drastic temperature rise during operation.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们今天无法做到这一点，因为 HBM 中使用的介电材料（例如 SiO2）是一种非常差的热导体，会在逻辑和存储器之间捕获热量，并导致运行期间温度急剧上升。

sentences.en: Similarly, there's many other materials in the GPU that are being re-evaluated today - 2 more examples are thermal interface materials and substrates.
sentences.zh: 同样，今天正在重新评估 GPU 中的许多其他材料 - 另外两个例子是热界面材料和基板。

sentences.en: However, getting a new material into a fab takes years and hundreds of millions of dollars of research - the infamous "lab-to-fab valley of death".At Discovered Materials, we're optimistic that AI agents can reduce the timeline and cost required to introduce new materials into semiconductor chips.
sentences.zh: 然而，将新材料引入晶圆厂需要数年时间和数亿美元的研究，即臭名昭著的“从实验室到晶圆厂的死亡之谷”。在 Discovered Materials，我们乐观地认为人工智能代理可以缩短将新材料引入半导体芯片所需的时间和成本。

sentences.en: We're seeing glimpses of this already - we tested 7 models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Kimi, and found that they're all able to computationally discover new materials that are dynamically stable and possess promising properties.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了这一点 - 我们测试了来自 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Kimi 的 7 个模型，发现它们都能够通过计算发现动态稳定且具有有前景的特性的新材料。

sentences.en: This was surprising to us - it would generally take a PhD student a couple of weeks of work to discover the kind of materials that these models find over an 8 hour run!However, computational discovery is the easy part.
sentences.zh: 这让我们感到惊讶 - 博士生通常需要几周的时间才能发现这些模型在 8 小时运行中找到的材料类型！然而，计算发现是容易的部分。

sentences.en: A material discovery is only valid if the material can be made and tested in a lab (As an example, graphene’s properties were predicted in 1947 but it was made for the first time in 2004).
sentences.zh: 仅当材料可以在实验室中制造和测试时，材料发现才是有效的（例如，石墨烯的特性在 1947 年就被预测到，但它是在 2004 年首次被制造出来的）。

sentences.en: Today’s models are not good at coming up with synthesis recipes to make materials in a lab.
sentences.zh: 今天的模型不擅长提出在实验室中制造材料的合成配方。

sentences.en: Even if they do get better at it, we're uncertain about how much that will help - making a new material is a highly empirical process involving trial and error over many experiments.
sentences.zh: 即使他们确实在这方面做得更好，我们也不确定这会有多大帮助——制造新材料是一个高度经验化的过程，涉及多次实验的反复试验。

sentences.en: Human experts themselves cannot "one-shot" the task, but we expect that a highly capable model will reduce the number of experimental iterations required to make a new material.
sentences.zh: 人类专家本身无法“一次性”完成这项任务，但我们期望一个高性能的模型将减少制造新材料所需的实验迭代次数。

sentences.en: We’ve seen some evidence of this over the 3 months of our Y Combinator batch - we simulated, synthesized and tested thermal interface materials (TIMs) that match the performance of TIMs the world's largest chemical companies have guarded as trade secrets for over 20 years.We’re releasing hundreds of hundreds of new materials discovered by frontier AI models, as well as our benchmark which measures model ability on material discovery here (also linked in the thread url): https://discoveredmaterials.com/research. It covers what we discuss above, as well as a variety of strange behavior that we observe from the models, such as Claude's propensity to reward hack or GPT-5.6 occasionally losing its mind after ~50M tokens.Our business model: We aim to license and sell IP on the materials we discover, as well as the IP on how to make these materials.
sentences.zh: 在我们的 Y Combinator 批次的 3 个月里，我们已经看到了一些证据 - 我们模拟、合成和测试了热界面材料 (TIM)，其性能与世界上最大的化学公司作为商业秘密保守了 20 多年的 TIM 的性能相匹配。我们将发布由前沿 AI 模型发现的数百种新材料，以及衡量模型材料发现能力的基准（也在线程 URL 中链接）：https://discoveredmaterials.com/research。它涵盖了我们上面讨论的内容，以及我们从模型中观察到的各种奇怪行为，例如 Claude 奖励黑客的倾向或 GPT-5.6 在大约 5000 万代币后偶尔会失去理智。我们的商业模式：我们的目标是许可和出售我们发现的材料的知识产权，以及如何制作这些材料的知识产权。

sentences.en: We're also exploring an alternate business model where we sell the harness+tools we use to discover materials to semiconductor and chemical companies, allowing them to discover materials on their own.
sentences.zh: 我们还在探索另一种商业模式，将用于发现材料的线束+工具出售给半导体和化学公司，使他们能够自己发现材料。

sentences.en: We're leaning towards the latter to start, but we expect that we'll do both in the long run.Our backstory: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford University, and has spent the last 11 years studying new materials for semiconductor chips.
sentences.zh: 我们一开始倾向于后者，但从长远来看，我们预计两者都会做。我们的背景故事：Akash 拥有斯坦福大学材料科学博士学位，在过去 11 年里一直在研究半导体芯片的新材料。

sentences.en: His work on new nanoscale interconnects was Stanford Engineering’s most popular story of 2025.
sentences.zh: 他在新型纳米级互连方面的工作是斯坦福大学工程学院 2025 年最受欢迎的故事。

sentences.en: Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and was a research engineer building video models and agents at Persona AI (acquired) and Luma Labs.We are very interested in your opinion!
sentences.zh: Advaith 在卡内基梅隆大学学习人工智能，并且是在 Persona AI（被收购）和 Luma Labs 构建视频模型和代理的研究工程师。我们对您的意见非常感兴趣！

sentences.en: The semiconductor industry is quite secretive, and your thoughts on the roadmap of the industry or the materials we should go after would be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 半导体行业相当神秘，您对行业路线图或我们应该追求的材料的想法将会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: We would also love to hear from people who have run experiments in labs - what can we learn from your experience doing empirical science?
sentences.zh: 我们也很想听听在实验室进行过实验的人的意见——我们可以从您进行实证科学的经验中学到什么？

blocks.html_en: Hey HN, we're Advaith and Akash from Discovered Materials ( https://discoveredmaterials.com/ ). We build AI agents that discover new materials for the semiconductor industry.

sentences.en: We build AI agents that discover new materials for the semiconductor industry.
sentences.zh: 我们构建人工智能代理，为半导体行业发现新材料。

blocks.html_en: GPUs today have a heat problem. Nvidia & AMD are almost doubling the TDP (Thermal Design Power) in every chip they release - the H100 (released 2022) has a TDP of 700W, Blackwell (2024) gives out 1.2 kW and Rubin (2026) gives out at 2.3 kW of heat. This trend is expected to continue, and getting rid of this heat is one of the major reasons datacenters consume so much power and water today - they need it to keep chips cool during operation.

blocks.html_en: The amount of heat produced by a chip and its ability to dissipate it are both influenced by the materials used to make it. For example, we could reduce the energy per bit required to move data between logic and memory by 10-50x by 3D packaging chips (placing HBM memory stacks directly on top of logic chips, instead of placing them beside logic on a 2D circuit board). However, we're unable to do this today because the dielectric material used in HBM (such as SiO2) is a very poor thermal conductor, trapping heat between logic and memory and causing drastic temperature rise during operation. Similarly, there's many other materials in the GPU that are being re-evaluated today - 2 more examples are thermal interface materials and substrates. However, getting a new material into a fab takes years and hundreds of millions of dollars of research - the infamous "lab-to-fab valley of death".

blocks.html_en: At Discovered Materials, we're optimistic that AI agents can reduce the timeline and cost required to introduce new materials into semiconductor chips. We're seeing glimpses of this already - we tested 7 models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Kimi, and found that they're all able to computationally discover new materials that are dynamically stable and possess promising properties. This was surprising to us - it would generally take a PhD student a couple of weeks of work to discover the kind of materials that these models find over an 8 hour run!

blocks.html_en: However, computational discovery is the easy part. A material discovery is only valid if the material can be made and tested in a lab (As an example, graphene’s properties were predicted in 1947 but it was made for the first time in 2004). Today’s models are not good at coming up with synthesis recipes to make materials in a lab. Even if they do get better at it, we're uncertain about how much that will help - making a new material is a highly empirical process involving trial and error over many experiments. Human experts themselves cannot "one-shot" the task, but we expect that a highly capable model will reduce the number of experimental iterations required to make a new material. We’ve seen some evidence of this over the 3 months of our Y Combinator batch - we simulated, synthesized and tested thermal interface materials (TIMs) that match the performance of TIMs the world's largest chemical companies have guarded as trade secrets for over 20 years.

blocks.html_en: We’re releasing hundreds of hundreds of new materials discovered by frontier AI models, as well as our benchmark which measures model ability on material discovery here (also linked in the thread url): https://discoveredmaterials.com/research. It covers what we discuss above, as well as a variety of strange behavior that we observe from the models, such as Claude's propensity to reward hack or GPT-5.6 occasionally losing its mind after ~50M tokens.

blocks.html_en: Our business model: We aim to license and sell IP on the materials we discover, as well as the IP on how to make these materials. We're also exploring an alternate business model where we sell the harness+tools we use to discover materials to semiconductor and chemical companies, allowing them to discover materials on their own. We're leaning towards the latter to start, but we expect that we'll do both in the long run.

content_html_zh: 推出 HN：Discovered Materials (YC P26) – 人工智能代理发现新材料 (discoveredmaterials.com)advaith08 22 小时前 132 分 |隐藏 |过去|最喜欢 | 28 条评论嘿 HN，我们是来自 Discovered Materials (https://discoveredmaterials.com/) 的 Advaith 和 Akash。 我们构建人工智能代理，为半导体行业发现新材料。当今的 GPU 存在散热问题。 Nvidia 和 AMD 几乎将其发布的每款芯片的 TDP（热设计功耗）提高了一倍 - H100（2022 年发布）的 TDP 为 700W，Blackwell（2024 年）的 TDP 为 1.2 kW，Rubin（2026 年）的 TDP 为 2.3 kW。 这种趋势预计将持续下去，而消除这种热量是当今数据中心消耗大量电力和水的主要原因之一——他们需要它来保持芯片在运行过程中冷却。芯片产生的热量及其散发热量的能力都受到制造它的材料的影响。 例如，我们可以通过 3D 封装芯片（将 HBM​​ 内存堆栈直接放置在逻辑芯片顶部，而不是将它们放置在 2D 电路板上的逻辑旁边）将逻辑和内存之间移动数据所需的每比特能量减少 10-50 倍。 然而，我们今天无法做到这一点，因为 HBM 中使用的介电材料（例如 SiO2）是一种非常差的热导体，会在逻辑和存储器之间捕获热量，并导致运行期间温度急剧上升。 同样，今天正在重新评估 GPU 中的许多其他材料 - 另外两个例子是热界面材料和基板。 然而，将新材料引入晶圆厂需要数年时间和数亿美元的研究，即臭名昭著的“从实验室到晶圆厂的死亡之谷”。在 Discovered Materials，我们乐观地认为人工智能代理可以缩短将新材料引入半导体芯片所需的时间和成本。 我们已经看到了这一点 - 我们测试了来自 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Kimi 的 7 个模型，发现它们都能够通过计算发现动态稳定且具有有前景的特性的新材料。 这让我们感到惊讶 - 博士生通常需要几周的时间才能发现这些模型在 8 小时运行中找到的材料类型！然而，计算发现是容易的部分。 仅当材料可以在实验室中制造和测试时，材料发现才是有效的（例如，石墨烯的特性在 1947 年就被预测到，但它是在 2004 年首次被制造出来的）。 今天的模型不擅长提出在实验室中制造材料的合成配方。 即使他们确实在这方面做得更好，我们也不确定这会有多大帮助——制造新材料是一个高度经验化的过程，涉及多次实验的反复试验。 人类专家本身无法“一次性”完成这项任务，但我们期望一个高性能的模型将减少制造新材料所需的实验迭代次数。 在我们的 Y Combinator 批次的 3 个月里，我们已经看到了一些证据 - 我们模拟、合成和测试了热界面材料 (TIM)，其性能与世界上最大的化学公司作为商业秘密保守了 20 多年的 TIM 的性能相匹配。我们将发布由前沿 AI 模型发现的数百种新材料，以及衡量模型材料发现能力的基准（也在线程 URL 中链接）：https://discoveredmaterials.com/research。它涵盖了我们上面讨论的内容，以及我们从模型中观察到的各种奇怪行为，例如 Claude 奖励黑客的倾向或 GPT-5.6 在大约 5000 万代币后偶尔会失去理智。我们的商业模式：我们的目标是许可和出售我们发现的材料的知识产权，以及如何制作这些材料的知识产权。 我们还在探索另一种商业模式，将用于发现材料的线束+工具出售给半导体和化学公司，使他们能够自己发现材料。 我们一开始倾向于后者，但从长远来看，我们预计两者都会做。我们的背景故事：Akash 拥有斯坦福大学材料科学博士学位，在过去 11 年里一直在研究半导体芯片的新材料。 他在新型纳米级互连方面的工作是斯坦福大学工程学院 2025 年最受欢迎的故事。 Advaith 在卡内基梅隆大学学习人工智能，并且是在 Persona AI（被收购）和 Luma Labs 构建视频模型和代理的研究工程师。我们对您的意见非常感兴趣！ 半导体行业相当神秘，您对行业路线图或我们应该追求的材料的想法将会非常有帮助。 我们也很想听听在实验室进行过实验的人的意见——我们可以从您进行实证科学的经验中学到什么？ 帮助
